text:
maria (Support): Heads-up: AcmeHealth escalated — their Next.js app started getting 401s in prod only after we shipped 1.3.1. Local dev and staged serverless preview work. Customer says bundling + edge runtime strips auth header or resolves to wrong package entry. They reported spike in retries and latency.
alex (DevEx): Can you paste the minimal repro, package.json exports, and the SDK version they have pinned? Also which bundler / node version on Vercel? :eyes:
maria (Support): SDK v1.3.1 (they say v1.2.0 worked). Running Next 13.4, Node 18.x on Vercel edge function. Their package.json exports block attached below (redacted):
```json
{
  "name": "acme-frontend",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk-js": "^1.3.1"
  },
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
    },
    "./runtime": {
      "import": "./dist/runtime.mjs",
      "require": "./dist/runtime.cjs"
    }
  }
}
```
maria (Support): They do a deep import `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js/runtime'` in an edge route. In prod the import resolves to the mjs entry, which is fine, but the edge runtime appears to strip the Authorization header when the SDK is used (we see 401s from our API proxy). Local Node server (CJS) uses index.cjs and works.
devon (Eng Runtime): Edge runtimes can rewrite imports and sometimes the bundler inlines small modules — could be a side-effect of using a different export subpath (`./runtime`). Any chance the bundler replaced the runtime with a browser-targeted shim that drops fetch headers? Need the built artifact (dist/) or a minimal repo.
toni (Eng-ML): Also check if the SDK's ESM build uses `globalThis.fetch` vs a custom fetch wrapper. On edge, Vercel sometimes polyfills fetch differently and header mutations can be lost on retries.
alex (DevEx): Quick repro suggestion: create a tiny repo with only Next route + `@redwood/sdk-js` import and reproduce on Vercel preview. If it fails there we can bisect. Can you ask for the `dist/runtime.mjs` top-of-file header (the export map entry) and the exact import path string they use? 
maria (Support): Customer supplied snippet:
```js
// app/api/ai/route.ts (edge)
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js/runtime'

export const runtime = 'edge'

export async function GET(req) {
  const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
  const r = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(r), { status: 200 })
}
```
maria (Support): Error observed in prod logs (our gateway):
```
2026-03-10T18:12:02Z proxy: request id=abc123 status=401 body="Unauthorized"
stack: Error: auth missing
    at sendRequest (dist/runtime.mjs:420:15)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues:95:5)
```
devon (Eng Runtime): That stack line indicates the ESM bundle path, ok. Two hypotheses: (1) bundler removed the env var or it's undefined in edge (but they pass key), (2) our ESM runtime uses a fetch wrapper that relies on Node header mutation semantics not available in the edge polyfill, causing the Authorization header to be dropped right before the outbound request. Curious that v1.2.0 worked — what changed between 1.2.0 and 1.3.1 around runtime exports?
alex (DevEx): I looked at the changelog: v1.3.0 introduced a unified ESM-only runtime and added a `./runtime` subpath in exports to encourage deep imports. That could have created dual module resolution paths for bundlers.
dan (Oncall): We rolled out a hotfix last week that changed the runtime wrapper to use `new Request()` instead of `fetch(url, { headers })` to preserve headers across redirects. If their environment polyfills Request differently it could affect header preservation. Any chance the edge runtime is rewriting requests and dropping the Authorization during an internal redirect (302->fetch)?
maria (Support): Customer reported spikes in retries — they see client-side retry loop hitting our 429/500 fallback, then auth fails. I'm attaching a small zip they sent (we have the dist/ artifacts). They said `dist/runtime.mjs` starts with `export * from './runtime-shim.js'` in the published package.
alex (DevEx): Ok, two immediate repro tasks for us:
1) Try running the published package (v1.3.1) in a minimal Next edge route in Vercel preview to see if we can reproduce Authorization being dropped.
2) Run the same import but force resolution to `require('@redwood/sdk-js')` path to use CJS path in a server Node 18 environment — see if behavior differs.
devon (Eng Runtime): If we reproduce, patch options:
- Add an explicit `./runtime/edge` entry in exports that points to an edge-tested shim so bundlers don't pick the browser-targeted file.
- Revert the Request wrapper change in the immediate hotfix and publish v1.3.2 as a potential rollback.
toni (Eng-ML): Also add an integration test that runs on a Vercel-like edge (within CI using `vercel dev` or a wasm-based polyfill) to catch this earlier.
maria (Support): Customer gave reproduce steps (short):
1) Next 13 app with `edge` route.
2) `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js/runtime'`
3) Deploy to Vercel with Node 18, run a few requests — observe some 401s and header missing traces.
alex (DevEx): Could be a packaging mismatch: some bundlers prefer `exports['./runtime']` over `exports['.']` and will tree-shake or rewrite; also some packagers use `sideEffects: false` and drop important polyfill code if not referenced. Check package.json `sideEffects` in the published package.
maria (Support): I asked the customer to temporarily pin 1.2.0 and confirm if that resolves. They're testing now.
deploy-bot: deploy logged: act/deploy/v1 -> site=acme-frontend env=prod ver=2026-03-10T17:50Z status=success
maria (Support): Customer confirmed pinning to 1.2.0 removed 401s (so far) — they reported all good for 10 minutes of testing. They're willing to hold on prod while we investigate.
devon (Eng Runtime): Good repro differential. Action items:
- I'll try to reproduce using v1.3.1 published package and Vercel edge preview today. (devon)
- If reproduced, prepare v1.3.2 rollback that reverts Request wrapper and add explicit `./runtime/edge` export. (devon + alex)
- Add CI vercel-edge test to catch this. (toni)
alex (DevEx): Also we should add guidance in docs on deep imports: recommend `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk-js'` instead of `/runtime` deep import for edge routes until we ship the edge-targeted entry.
maria (Support): I'm sending the customer a status update: thanks for being patient. I'll link this thread and assign to eng runtime to prioritize. :pray:
devon (Eng Runtime): I'll update once I have a repro. If anyone sees similar reports from other customers please tag this thread. :mag:
maria (Support): Marking as P1-escalation internally until rollback or patch. 
alex (DevEx): Note for release: when we ship v1.3.2 include a note about package `exports` and edge entry to avoid future bundler ambiguity.
maria (Support): Closing the loop here when we have a patch. Thanks all.
